edit.twofaExplain: A password stops a sign-in that only has one SMS code.
edit.twofaHintWarn: Anyone attempting a sign-in sees the hint.
edit.twofaErrHintLeaks: The hint contains the password itself — anyone would see it
edit.twofaCreatedTitle: Password created. Save it — it will not be shown again.
edit.twofaCopyFailed: Copying failed — select the password and copy it by hand; there is no other copy.
edit.twofaCopyManual: The clipboard is unavailable here — select the password and copy it by hand.
edit.twofaStoreFailed: Telegram accepted the password but storing it in Telebuba failed. This is the only copy — copy it now: the password can no longer be changed or removed from here.
edit.twofaUnconfirmed: The connection dropped before Telegram answered, so this password may or may not have been applied. It is the only copy — copy it now, then reopen the card to see which way it went.
edit.twofaUnconfirmedChange: The connection dropped before Telegram answered. Either the previous password (still stored here) or this new one is now in force — check on the phone. This is the only copy of the new one.
edit.twofaUnconfirmedKept: The connection dropped before Telegram answered, and the state could not be read afterwards. The previous password is still stored here, but which one is in force — it, this new one, or neither — cannot be told from here: check on the phone. This is the only copy of the new one.
edit.twofaNotStoredNote: Without the stored password Telegram authorises no change, no removal, and neither attaching nor detaching a recovery address. An attachment already under way can still be finished: confirm the code, have it mailed again, or cancel it.
edit.twofaDisableBody: Without a cloud password the account can be taken over with an SMS code alone again.
edit.twofaStoredStale: Telegram has no cloud password, but one is still stored here.
edit.twofaForgetBody: Telegram has no cloud password for this account, so the stored copy guards nothing. Deleting it only clears it from Telebuba.
edit.twofaForgetUnknownBody: The 2FA state could not be read, so nothing is changed on Telegram: only the copy stored here is deleted. If Telegram does hold a cloud password it stays, and it can no longer be changed or removed from here.
edit.twofaEmailWarn: Whoever gets into that mailbox can reset the password and take the account.
edit.twofaEmailErrShape: An address of the form name@domain is required.
edit.twofaEmailUnlinkBody: Recovering the password by email becomes impossible: forget the password and the account is gone.
edit.twofaEmailCancelBody: The address will not be attached and the code already mailed stops working.

logEventHint.neurocomment_no_account_available: No account in the campaign can post in this channel. The exact reason is next to the row. Clears on its own: "account paused", "re-joining the chat after losing access", "no data yet: the account has not been onboarded to this channel" (onboarding reaches the pair on a later pass) and "join by request: waiting for an admin to approve" (if it is never approved, the whole channel leaves the campaign). Yours to set: "per-account hourly limit reached" — "Comments per hour (per account)"; "per-channel daily limit reached" — "Comments per day per channel"; "the account is not warmed up, or its Trust-score is below the threshold" — warming, or "Min. trust-score to run"; "warming has not handed the account over to neurocomment yet" — the Warming page; "the account was taken off this channel by the operator". Needs attention: "chat restricted: a mute, an unconfirmed ban, or a captcha not passed", "joining the chat failed", "the account is banned in the channel's chat", "join attempts used up", "no accounts linked" and "the account is in the chat but not commenting: no more specific reason" — link another account, or link the channel again.
logEventHint.neurocomment_posted_row_missing: The comment reached Telegram, but its row in our history was not saved. The comment itself is live in the channel — we simply will not show it in the feed, will not count it towards the limits, and will not notice if it gets deleted. By the app's own logic this cannot happen, which is why the row is flagged as an error: there is nothing to fix by hand, but the failure is worth reporting to the developers.
logEventHint.neurocomment_generation_retry: The previous text did not fit: too long or too short, blocked by the filter, or a repeat of a comment we already sent. We are writing this same post again — the counter next to the row says which repeat it is and how many are allowed. No action needed: if nothing fits, a "Text generation failed" row next to it gives the reason.
logEventHint.neurocomment_generation_exhausted: The AI produced no acceptable text. Beside the reason is which generator answered and what it said: DeepSeek writes the text, Gemini handles caption-less photo posts. Check that provider's key, the campaign prompt, and the rate limit.
logEventHint.neurocomment_challenge_attempt: The AI read the captcha and is sending its answer to the bot. The counter next to the row says which attempt this is and how many are allowed: if the bot asks again, we answer once more. No action needed.
logEventHint.neurocomment_challenge_result: How the captcha ended is written next to the row. "Passed": the account can comment on the channel. "AI request limit": the pair is queued nowhere and we retry later on our own — nothing to do. Every other outcome the engine finishes by itself: the pair gets a second and last attempt within five minutes, and if that one fails too the account leaves this discussion chat and never returns to the channel. There is nothing to press — the "Captcha solving" block only shows who the engine is working on right now. If this keeps happening across channels, check the model and the key in settings.
logEventHint.neurocomment_post_skipped: There is nothing to comment on: a repost, an empty post, a bare link, or a file there is nothing to say about. The exact reason is written next to the row. A photo with no caption IS commented on — the account looks at the picture.
logEventHint.neurocomment_post_unavailable: The comment never reached Telegram: the connection failed — proxy, session, or a timeout. The account did nothing wrong, so it gets no pause and keeps working in this channel. Check the proxy and the session, not the account.
logEventHint.neurocomment_comment_deleted: The channel removed our comment — moderation or a ban. Check the channel/account.
logEventHint.neurocomment_post_cooldown: A pause from Telegram: it asks us to wait, slow mode, a premium limit, or a spam limit. The account stops commenting for a while; the exact cause is in the row next to it.
logEventHint.neurocomment_post_gated: The chat will not let this account write: a captcha was not passed, or an admin muted it or closed the chat to non-members. The account is taken off this channel until it is connected again, and the channel itself is charged a write failure — three in a row and the channel goes on pause.
logEventHint.neurocomment_post_ban_unconfirmed: Telegram refused this account's comment in the channel's chat, but no ban by that chat was confirmed. A refusal counts only when the chat's own record lets this account write and @SpamBot sees no limit on it: a counted one carries the counter, without a counter nothing is spent — check the account's spam status there. Counted at most once a day; on the second counted refusal, roughly a day after the first, the account leaves the chat and is taken off the channel. The count expires after 48 hours, and a delivered comment clears it.
logEventHint.neurocomment_group_ban_unconfirmed: We asked the channel's chat whether it holds a personal write ban on this account — it does not. So a channel ban is not the cause: it is the account itself, a captcha, or the chat's own settings. Nothing to do here — this line explains the one next to it. A refusal like this is no ban on its own, but it is counted, and on the second counted refusal the account does leave the chat; a separate line about the ban appears next to it then.
logEventHint.neurocomment_account_banned: The account left the channel's chat and no longer posts there. One of two things happened: Telegram confirmed an admin's ban outright, or the account was refused a write twice — such refusals are counted at most once a day, and only where the chat's own record lets this account write and @SpamBot sees no limit on it. The outcome is the same: this channel is closed to this account. The other accounts keep working in this channel. If the channel matters, add another account to the campaign. If every account falls out this way, the channel leaves the campaign on its own.
logEventHint.neurocomment_group_ban_confirmed: Both checks agreed: this group holds a personal write ban on the account, and @SpamBot says the account itself is fine. So a channel admin banned us — we left the chat rather than sit where we are not welcome.
logEventHint.neurocomment_group_ban_account_limited: Telegram blocked the write, but @SpamBot reports the account limited across all groups — this channel did not ban it. While the limit holds the account cannot post anywhere. Let it rest: on the Warming page press "Back to warming". Check again in a few days — account card, "Spam/ban signals" block, "Check" button.
logEventHint.neurocomment_channel_all_accounts_banned: Every account serving this channel is now banned in its chat, so the channel was unlinked from the campaign and the listener stopped watching it. Link it again after adding an account that can post there.
logEventHint.neurocomment_post_access_lost: The account can no longer reach this channel's discussion chat — kicked, or the group went private. The pair is parked and re-joins itself: one attempt within minutes, then one a day, two in total.
logEventHint.neurocomment_rejoin_attempt: The account lost access to the discussion chat and is trying to get back in: the first attempt within minutes, then one a day, two in total. If no account gets back, the channel leaves the campaign — no sooner than two days from now.
logEventHint.neurocomment_rejoin_gave_up: This account used up every re-join attempt for the channel's chat (one a day, two in total) and is no longer in it — the channel is closed for this account, and the board now badges it «Join attempts exhausted». The account keeps working on the campaign's other channels, and the channel's other accounts keep working here. Time alone buys it no further attempts: the count only resets if the account does get into the chat, or if you link the channel again. If every account drops out this way, the channel leaves the campaign on its own.
logEventHint.neurocomment_channel_rejoin_exhausted: Every account serving this channel used up its re-join attempts (one a day, two in total) and none of them can post there, so the channel was unlinked from the campaign and the listener stopped watching it. Link it again once an account can get into its chat.
logEventHint.neurocomment_channel_join_impossible: Telegram says this channel's address does not exist — a username nobody owns, or an invite link that has been revoked. Nothing can join it, so it was unlinked from the campaign without spending the re-join attempts and the listener stopped watching it. Check the address and link the channel again.
logEventHint.neurocomment_captcha_retry: The chat's guardian bot did not let the account through, so the captcha solver gets a second — and last — try. The counter next to the row shows which try this is out of the whole budget: the first one happened when the account entered the chat. Nothing to do; the retry starts on its own within five minutes. If it fails too, the account leaves the chat and never comes back to it.
logEventHint.neurocomment_captcha_gave_up: Both captcha attempts are used up, so the account left this channel's discussion chat and will not join it again. The counter next to the row closes the count. The decision is final: neither a restart nor another onboarding pass undoes it. The channel stays in the campaign for as long as any other account still works there.
logEventHint.neurocomment_channel_captcha_unsolved: No account serving this channel got past the guardian bot's captcha: each had two tries and all of them left the chat. The channel was unlinked from the campaign and the listener stopped watching it. Link it again if the solver learns to pass this bot, or once you have an account the bot will let through.
logEventHint.neurocomment_captcha_review_failed: The list of pairs stuck on a captcha could not be read, so this pass checked nothing. The other passes ran as usual and nothing is lost: the list is re-read every five minutes. If the line keeps coming back, check the error type next to it.
logEventHint.neurocomment_channel_comments_off: The channel has no discussion chat: its owner switched comments off. There is nothing to post to and nowhere to join, so the channel is unlinked from the campaign right away — the next line. Link it again if the owner turns comments back on.
logEventHint.neurocomment_channel_comments_off_droppe: The channel was unlinked from the campaign and the listener stopped watching it: its comments are disabled. No account joined or left anything — there was nothing to join. Link the channel again once it has a discussion chat.
logEventHint.neurocomment_channel_paused: The channel refused our comments three times in a row, so it is paused for a day: nothing posts there and no account is connected to it. There are two rounds, and the last one still serves its full day: the channel leaves the campaign not when the second round ends, but when that day runs out — no sooner than 48 hours after the first round. One delivered comment clears the count. The pause can run longer than that: the channel is not dropped until every account has tried it.
logEventHint.neurocomment_channel_dropped: The channel refused our comments through every pause round (one a day, two in total) and then sat out the last window too — no sooner than 48 hours after the first round, not the moment that round ended. It was unlinked from the campaign and the listener stopped watching it. Nobody left its chat — the block is the channel's, not a ban on an account. Link it again if it starts accepting comments.
logEventHint.neurocomment_onboard_join_by_request: This channel's chat only admits by request — the request is sent and the admin decides from here. The counter next to the row says which request this is and how many are allowed; the next one goes out no sooner than a day later, because an admin reads a re-request as spam. No action needed: if nobody approves it, the channel leaves the campaign and a "Channel dropped: join request never approved" row appears next to it. Only the channel's admin can speed this up.
logEventHint.neurocomment_onboard_join_request_pendin: A request is already out, so this pass does not repeat it — we are waiting for the admin. The counter next to the row says how many of the allowed requests have gone out; on the last one this line repeats every pass until the admin decides. No action needed: either the request is approved, or the channel leaves the campaign.
logEventHint.neurocomment_join_request_expired: Nobody approved our join requests to this channel's chat (two requests, a day apart), so the channel was unlinked from the campaign and the listener stopped watching it. Link it again once an admin is ready to approve the accounts.
logEventHint.neurocomment_listener_access_lost: The listener fell out of this channel, so its posts will not arrive until it is back. The loss is counted and the listener re-joins on this same pass; the counter next to the row says which loss this is and how many are allowed. No action needed. Once they run out the listener leaves the channel alone and a "Listener gave up re-joining channel" row appears next to it. Losses are counted over a rolling week, so occasional blips do not add up.
logEventHint.neurocomment_listener_rejoin_exhausted: The allowed losses are used up: the listener no longer re-joins this channel, new posts from it will not arrive, and there will be nothing to comment on. The counter next to the row shows the whole budget and closes the count. The channel itself is not dropped from the campaign and no account is taken off it. Neither a restart nor linking the channel again undoes this: the count expires on its own a week after the last loss, and the listener tries again then.
logEventHint.neurocomment_channel_cooled: The post was skipped because the channel is paused right now after write errors. This is the only line about this post: nobody wrote a comment. The pause ends on its own — the channel goes back to work, or, on its last round, leaves the campaign instead. Deleted comments never cause a pause: the channel clears them out and we still comment on its next post.
logEventHint.neurocomment_no_campaign: No active campaign for this channel.
logEventHint.neurocomment_channel_inactive_dropped: The channel published nothing for longer than the configured window — confirmed by asking Telegram, not inferred from our own silence. The reason column carries how many days it stayed quiet. Only a dated post older than the window retires a channel; a failed or empty read decides nothing. The channel was unlinked from the campaign, the listener stopped watching it, and the comment authors left its discussion group. The listener's own subscription is left alone: dropping it honestly means stamping the standing join as lost, and that stamp spends a re-join budget which must be intact if you link the channel again. Link it again if it comes back to life.
logEventHint.neurocomment_channel_posts_missed: Our records showed silence, but Telegram reported recent posts. So the channel is fine and our subscription is not: the listener never received them. The channel stays in the campaign and its last-post stamp was repaired, so it will not be dropped. If this keeps appearing for the same channel, check that the listener account is still a member.
logEventHint.neurocomment_channel_activity_unknown: The last-post read failed, so no verdict was reached: the channel stays in the campaign and is re-checked on the next pass. A one-off line is ordinary network noise. Hours of them mean the listener account has trouble reaching this channel specifically.

accounts.title: Accounts
accounts.hint: Every role in the dialogue speaks from its own account, so a campaign needs at least two. An account held by warming, by neurocomment or by another running campaign cannot be picked until it is free.

scenario.title: Scenario configuration

mode.label: Campaign mode
mode.hint: A campaign walks the target chats and acts the dialogue out once in each. Reviving keeps one chat alive with a fresh dialogue every cycle.

topic.label: Topic
topic.placeholder: What the accounts should be talking about
topic.hint: The brief the model writes from. It is stored on the campaign, so a generation always runs on the topic that was last saved.

generate.hint: Generation writes all of it at once: the role names, how each of them speaks, and the text of every message — from the topic above. Whatever is already there gets replaced. One run writes at most 12 steps, because the answer has to fit whole; the dialogue can be extended by hand.

unique.label: Unique wording per account
unique.hint: Each account says the same thing in its own words, so the identical text is not posted across every target chat.

context.label: Read the chat before writing
context.hint: The accounts read the last messages of the target chat and answer in its tone. Chat text is untrusted input and is fenced before it reaches the model.

media.label: Media message link
media.hint: A link to the message whose photo or video one step of the dialogue carries. Leave it empty for a text-only dialogue.

roles.title: Roles
roles.hint: A role is a persona: its description IS the prompt the account speaks from. Every role needs an account of its own before the campaign can start.
roles.name: Name of role {{position}}

steps.title: Dialogue
steps.hint: The list order is the dialogue order. A reply or a reaction may only point at a step above it: that message has to be in the chat already. A reaction cannot be pointed at — it is not a message in the chat, so it stays disabled in the list.

scenario.approveHint: Save the scenario before approving it.

preview.title: Approve the scenario
preview.unsaved: Unsaved edits — the preview shows the scenario as it is stored.
preview.none: Nothing to preview yet. Generate a dialogue or write one by hand.

setup.title: Campaign setup
setup.liveLocked: The campaign is running — settings cannot change. Stop the run first.

targets.label: Target chats
targets.hint: One chat per line: @name, a t.me link, or a t.me/+HASH invite. The accounts join each of them and play the dialogue once.

sequential.title: Sequential
sequential.body: Targets are visited one after another, with a pause between them.

parallel.title: Parallel
parallel.unavailable: Not available yet: a burst of joins into every chat at once is the most visible way to work there is.

pause.label: Pause between targets, sec
pause.hint: A minimum and a maximum, in SECONDS. Before each next target a random pause from that range is drawn.

perHour.label: Messages per hour
perHour.hint: Per account, over a sliding hour of its whole neuroshilling history. A step past the cap is skipped and the dialogue moves on.

perChat.label: Messages per chat per day
perChat.hint: Per account-and-chat pair. 0 means no ceiling.

total.label: Total per account
total.hint: A ceiling for the whole life of the campaign. Empty means no limit.

reserve.label: Reserve accounts
reserve.hint: Accounts marked as reserve play no role. When Telegram bans a playing account, the oldest reserve takes its role, joins the chat and carries on. A chat that refuses everyone spends no reserve.

autoresponder.label: Autoresponder
autoresponder.hintOff: After the dialogue the accounts neither read the chat nor reply. Turn on «Neurodialogue» — a free account keeps the conversation going.

replyToHumans.label: Reply to real people
replyToHumans.hint: The one place where a stranger's text influences what the accounts publish. Both settings are required: «Autoresponder: Neurodialog» and this switch.
replyToHumans.warning: Replies to real people are on. Chat text is written by strangers; the campaign brief never reaches the model call, and every answer is parsed for links, mentions, phone numbers and wallet addresses. An answer that echoes the message is dropped.
replyToHumans.caption: Without this the autoresponder publishes nothing
replyToHumans.idle: The autoresponder only reads the chat and spends AI requests — nothing is published.

listen.label: Listen to chat, min
listen.hint: How many minutes the accounts keep reading the chat after the dialogue has played out. Counted per target, and the targets are walked one at a time.

listening.title: Chat listening
listening.hint: Accounts read the target chat by polling it every half minute — one account per chat, no subscription. On its own this only fills the chat counters below; what is read becomes the context for replies once the autoresponder is answering too. Switched off, not a single extra request is made.
listening.caption: after the dialogue in every target

campaign.body: Play the scenario through the targets once

revive.body: Loop until stopped: dialogue → listening → pause

uniqueMessages.label: Distinct voices per role
uniqueMessages.caption: Generation only — the approved text is what reaches the chats

readChat.label: Read the target chat
readChat.caption: What is read feeds the reply context

steps.0: Create a campaign — it holds the topic, the target chats, the roster and the dialogue.
steps.1: Pick the accounts that will play the roles. An account may belong to several campaigns, but only one running campaign holds it at a time.
steps.2: Describe the topic, let the model draft the dialogue, edit it and approve it.
steps.3: Start the run: the accounts join every target chat and act the dialogue out with human-like pauses.

regenerate.title: Generate a new dialogue?
regenerate.body: The model writes a fresh dialogue and it replaces the stored one — every role, every step and every edit made by hand. The chosen media step is let go too: the lines will be different ones, and the old step number would point at the wrong line. This cannot be undone.
